provenance.source: PR #4121 "Coerce None values into strings in logentry params", squash-merged 2025-03-12; the fix commit e71ccbf19 reverts it and says why (fixes #4267)
provenance.note: introduced by this PR: the base passes record.args through untouched, and the PR replaces it with a tuple built by iterating record.args, which flattens a mapping argument to its keys. The fix commit reverts the hunk on 2025-04-14 and states the consequence: 'Because we iterate over `record.args`, that change caused us to only send the dictionary's keys, not the values.' By then the statement had moved to logging.py:268-272 (identical text), so the revert deletes the five lines this diff adds at a shifted line number, restores `"params": record.args,`, and adds two tests asserting the params are the dict.

keywords: only the mapping's keys reach the report
the values of a dictionary passed as arguments are lost
a mapping logged with percent placeholders keeps just its key names
dict arguments are flattened into their keys
the message renders with key names instead of the substituted values
mapping-style interpolation receives the key names
the interpolated parameters collapse to the dictionary keys
bugs.note: stdlib logging accepts a single mapping as record.args for %(name)s templates; the generator iterates it, so keys, not values, are sent. The generator also rewrites a None argument to the string "None", which was the PR's intent.
